transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm seeking help because I've been struggling with really extreme, long-lasting mood swings. For about 11 months, I was feeling incredibly energetic, hyperactive, and talkative, but then I crashed into a deep depression where I've felt completely exhausted and unmotivated for the last 9 months. It has been really hard to cope with this constant instability.
Have you ever had hallucinations or strong beliefs that others said weren’t true during times when your mood symptoms were not happening? If so, did that last for at least 2 weeks?
No, I have never experienced hallucinations or those kinds of strong beliefs, especially not when my mood was normal. My mind has always felt clear in that way.
During that high-energy period, did your symptoms ever get so severe that you were hospitalized, had major problems at work or with other people, or did risky things that caused serious consequences?

I was definitely extremely active, talkative, and busy during that time, but it never led to hospitalization. I don't recall it ever causing any major disasters or severe consequences at work or with other people.
During that high-energy period, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested, like only a few hours a night without feeling tired?
I don't really recall having a decreased need for sleep during that time. I think I still slept a normal amount and didn't experience that feeling of being fully rested on just a few hours.
Before this 9-month depression, had you been feeling down or low most of the time for at least 2 years, or did the depression start more as a distinct episode after that high-energy period?

The depression definitely started as a distinct episode right after that high-energy phase, rather than a long-term low mood. I had that 11-month period of high energy and irritability, and then I crashed directly into this current 9-month depression.

During that high-energy period, did other people notice you were clearly different from your usual self, and did it cause a noticeable change in how well you functioned even if it didn’t lead to major consequences?

Yes, people definitely noticed a huge change because I was suddenly extremely social, talking constantly, and speaking very rapidly. My functioning changed quite a bit too, as I was constantly active and taking on way more work projects than usual, though it never got out of hand.
During that high-energy period, did you also have racing thoughts, feel unusually confident or grand, or get more easily distracted than usual?

Yes, my thoughts were spinning incredibly fast in my head, constantly jumping from one idea to another and making it hard to keep up. I didn't really feel unusually confident or easily distracted, but those racing thoughts were extremely prominent.
Was that 11-month high-energy period one continuous stretch, or did it include shorter episodes with times in between when your mood was back to normal?
I'm not quite sure, to be honest. I can't clearly remember if that whole 11-month period was completely continuous, or if there were brief moments where my mood went back to normal in between.
Even without hospitalization, during that high-energy time did your behavior ever become so extreme that others thought you were out of control or clearly unable to function normally?
I don't think my behavior ever got so extreme that I was completely out of control. Even though I was extremely active and talkative, I was still able to function and manage my daily life.
During that high-energy period, did you ever have hallucinations or unusually strong beliefs, like feeling you had special powers or were destined for something extraordinary?
No, I didn't experience any hallucinations during that high-energy period. I also never had any beliefs about having special powers or being destined for something extraordinary.
